messages.translation:
Stay in consensus: update to Nexa full node 2.2.0.0

Nexa is pushing forward with protocol improvements, and we recommend all users update their node client to the latest version.

This release includes a rolling checkpoint mechanism. Once a block reaches 200 confirmations in the chain, the node marks it as settled. From that depth on, the block's state stays unchanged and any subsequent reorg will be rejected.

For exchanges and services, this means: after 200 confirmations, a transaction cannot be reversed.

This is also the last release before the upcoming hard fork and the activation of the Tailstorm protocol. Staying in consensus and updating your client is critical. 👇

messages.text:
I am the Nexa Nifty Bot and I allow you to create, display and trade NFTs within Telegram.  Note you can (and should) open a private chat to me at @NexaNiftyBot and mostly talk to me there!
    
I STRONGLY prefer you to run Wally Wallet (for now!), which you can install on Android or iOS in from the Google or Apple store!  If you use a different wallet you will not be able to trade NFTs (yet).

FIRST!  Use '/nft register' (and scan the QR code) to register a Wally Wallet NEXA account with me.  This way I know your Nexa address!  If you are not using Wally wallet, use '/nft address <nexa address>' to manually enter an address.  Your wallet probably cannot "see" NFTs (unless its Wally Wallet).  But they will be in there...
    
Use '/nft mint "NFT title" "NFT collection"' and follow the instructions to create an NFT (you'll be asked to upload images).  If you upload multiple images at once, the order is: 
  1. the public image, 
  2. the card front,
  3. the card back,
  4. the private image.
You can upload just 2 or 3 images; rather than all 4.  If you upload 2 images, the first image will be both the public and front card face and the second will be the back.  

Here are some things you can ask me to do!

Use '/nft <id or title> [caption] [group name or title]' to display NFTs.  If we are in a Telegram Group, I show only the main image in the NFT.  If we are chatting privately I will show more info.
Use '/nfthide <id or title> <seconds> [caption] [group name or title]' to show the public contents for some seconds, and then show the back (if it exists) or delete the image.
Use '/nftflip <id or title> <seconds>' to show the front of the NFT for some seconds, and then show the public contents.
Use '/nftreveal <id or title> <seconds>' to show the back of the NFT for some seconds, and then show the public contents.
Use '/nftoffer <id or title> <amount in NEXA>' to make a firm offer to sell an NFT.  You then need to scan the provided QR code with Wally wallet and accept the resulting transaction after reading it to make sure it's doing what you expect.  
At that point, I will replace this message with your sell offer and buyers can scan it to purchase!
USe '/nftsearch <keyword>' to see up to 10 NFTs that match that keyword.
Use '/nftdetails <id or title>' to see details about an NFT.
Use '/nftforsale <max price>' to see NFTs for sale, and '/more' to move through the list.
Use '/nftbuy <id or title>' to put up a QR code that allows you to purchase a for-sale NFT.
Use '/nft address' to see what address you have registered.

Using no argument or 'it' refers to the NFT most recently referenced by you.
When a group of NFTs are shown, you can use their index (starting at 1) to reference them.  For example:
'/nftforsale'  (pretend 5 NFTs are shown)
'/nftdetails 3'  (let's see details about the 3rd one shown, pretend its for sale)
'/nftbuy it' (ok put up a QR code to purchase it)

If you see a QR code offer, you can scan it to purchase that NFT (in a decentralized, trustless, P2P, manner)!!  You can join the group https://t.me/Nexa_NFT_Trading to see all the offers!

If you reply to one of my messages, you can skip the "/nft" command prefix and which NFT we are talking about.  Just reply with "details", "buy", or "offer it <price>" for example.

messages.text:
硬件加速：基于电路的扩容

本系列的第二篇文章利用六个组件、一条磁带和一个读写头构建了 Nexa 的验证引擎，并演示了它如何在完全不运行软件的情况下，完成从 Alice 到 Bob 的一笔支付。

由于磁带始终只向一个方向移动，该引擎满足了“更优秀的比特币”所需具备的四个条件中的第一个：即支持流水线处理。

本文将探讨如何满足其余的条件。正如 Nexa 首席科学家 Peter Rizun 博士（@PeterRizun）在悉尼所展示的那样，我们只需进行三项简单的改动，就能完善中本聪的比特币并使其满足所有这些条件；在此过程中，该引擎还将几乎“零成本”地获得另外两项特性：可扩展性和可压缩性。

https://forum.nexa.org/t/scaling-by-circuit/1749
messages.translation:
Hardware acceleration: Scaling by circuit

The second article in this series builds Nexa's validation engine out of six components, a tape and a read/write head, and demonstrates how it completes a payment from Alice to Bob without running any software at all.

Because the tape only ever moves in one direction, the engine satisfies the first of the four conditions a "better Bitcoin" must meet: it supports pipelining.

This article explores how to meet the remaining conditions. As Nexa Chief Scientist Dr. Peter Rizun (@PeterRizun) showed in Sydney, we only need three simple changes to perfect Satoshi's Bitcoin and make it satisfy all of them; along the way the engine also gains two more properties at almost "zero cost": scalability and compressibility.

https://forum.nexa.org/t/scaling-by-circuit/1749

messages.text:
I'll fetch that Nexa forum thread and summarize it for you.# Nexa 论坛帖《Scaling By Circuit》总结

**来源**：https://forum.nexa.org/t/scaling-by-circuit/1749 （Nexa 官方论坛，硬件项目系列第二篇）
性质**：技术长文 + 配图（含 5 张架构示意图），核心是 **"用电路/硬件实现比特币式扩容" 的论证，主要论据来自 Nexa 首席科学家 Dr. Peter Rizun 2024 年 11 月悉尼 Australian Crypto Convention 的演讲。

---

## 一、全文主线：给"更好的比特币"打勾

系列第一篇用"六组件 + 磁带 + 磁头"把 Nexa 的验证引擎搭出来，证明它**可流水线化（pipelineable）**。本篇把剩下三个勾补齐，**只需三处改动**，顺带白送两个属性：

| 属性 | 来源 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| Pipelineable 可流水线 | 磁带单向流动 | 第一篇已证明 |
| Scalable 可扩容 | 并行流水线 + "集合树" | 本篇第 1 处改动 |
| Extensible 可扩展 | 反馈回路 → 图灵机 | 本篇衍生（意外收获） |
| Compressible 可压缩 | UTXO 承诺写进区块头 | 本篇第 2 处改动 |
| Incentive compatible 激励相容 | 哈希函数强制跑完验证流程 | 第一篇主题（第 3 处改动） |

---

## 二、四个技术要点

### 1. 两条流水线（并行化）——靠"反相时钟"解决竞态
- 加第二条并行验证流水线，用开关把交易路由到空闲的那条。
- 难点一：两个磁头共用同一个 UTXO 集，若同一时钟周期内都想花掉同一枚币，会**竞态**。
  - 解法（纯硬件）：**把第二条流水线的时钟信号反相**——一条在上升沿抓币，另一条在下降沿抓币，物理上不可能同时访问同一枚币。极简，但很优雅。

### 2. "集合树"替代 Merkle 树——本篇最关键的改动
- 难点二：并行后交易**出序可能与入序不同**（TX2 可能先于 TX1 进块）。对等节点重算出的根哈希不同 → 区块被判无效。
- 传统解法是**排序**，但排序不可流水线化（磁带要来回走）→ **排序无法扩容**。
- 作者主张：中本聪白皮书里的 "Merkle tree" 应被**字面之外的意图**理解——他要的不是"列表的树"而是**"集合的树"**。真正的答案是 **compact bitwise prefix tree（紧凑位前缀树）**：
  - 同样支持 SPV 证明；
  - 且**与交易顺序无关**——只要两个交易集合相等，根哈希就相等。
- 这建立在 **Amaury Séchet**（BCH 核心开发者）"把区块当集合而非列表来哈希"的思路之上。
- 有了它，**无需排序即可恢复可流水线化** → 一条改动就让币"可扩容"。

> 作者给出的扩容公式：流水线化下，TPS 上限 ≈ **最慢一步（通常是签名验证）耗时的倒数**，其他短延迟无关紧要；并行化下，吞吐可**乘以流水线条数**。Rizun 原话：*"基本上我们只要往问题上砸更多硬件，就能达到任意规模。"*

### 3. "意外的图灵机"——扩展性来自反馈回路
- 场景：Alice→Bob，Bob 立刻把同一枚币付给 Carol。因为顺序不可控，磁头可能**先**看到 Bob→Carol：查 UTXO 找不到该币，但也找不到"已花费"的证据 → **既不能判有效也不能判无效 = 未决（undecided）**。
- 解法：加**第三条流水线**把未决交易**回灌到输入端**。重入后 Bob 的币已被写入 UTXO 集，交易即可正常验证通过。
- 正是"存在未决状态"逼出了反馈路径，而反馈路径让机器**可模拟图灵机**：磁头能左右移动、能插入新格，磁带长度实际无界。
- 实用意义**：可**纯用脚本**加入量子抗性签名等新特性，**连软/硬分叉都不需要 → 币变得"可扩展"。

### 4. "用证明代替数据库"——可压缩性
- 现状：全验证节点必须自维护 UTXO 集来判断币是否未花费。
- 第 2 处改动：矿工把 UTXO 集存为紧凑位前缀树，**把该树根哈希放进区块头**（紧挨着区块根哈希）。
  - 思想源自 BitcoinTalk 2012 年"终极区块链压缩"帖。
  - 全节点此后只需**一条到区块头的分支证明**即可确认币未花费，**不再需要 UTXO 数据库**。
- 矿工计算 UTXO 根哈希不难：可流水线、可并行、每次增删 O(log s) 复杂度 → 符合"可扩容"定义。

---

## 三、UTXO 模型 vs 账户模型（Nexa vs 以太坊）

这是全文的收尾对比，也是"并行度从哪来"的根因：

| 维度 | Nexa（UTXO） | 以太坊（账户） |
|---|---|---|
| 状态模型 | 只有"币"，全花或全不花 | 账户 + 余额 |
| 状态改动范围 | **局部化**到指定输入 | 磁头身处全局状态空间，可读写一切 |
| 并行性 | **高**——可预知每笔交易能改的状态区域，多磁头无冲突 | **低**——交易可触及的状态区域无法局部化 |
| 风险 | 输入本质上是"防火墙" | 合约混乱时，Eve 可能写出扣 Alice 账户给 Eve 的交易 |
| 定位 | 币/商品，矿工 PoW 确认 | Ether 是"去中心化公司的股份"，非币非商品 |

作者结论：**两者是服务不同目的的两种东西**，不存在简单优劣。

---

## 四、总体结论

> "纸上，这台引擎已经完整了：一个更好的比特币，逐项打勾，由导线和门电路构成。剩下的就是把它用**你能握在手里的真硅**造出来——那正是本系列下一步的方向。"

**一句话**：这篇文章是用**电路级硬件架构**论证 Nexa 为何天然可扩容——**并行流水线（反相时钟）+ 集合树（免排序）+ UTXO 局部状态 + 反馈回路（图灵完备）+ 区块头 UTXO 承诺**，五者合力得到"可扩容、可扩展、可压缩、激励相容"的比特币改良方案，并预告下一篇进入**真实芯片实现**。

**引用来源**：Peter Rizun 悉尼演讲（2024-11-23）；BitcoinTalk 2012"终极区块链压缩"帖；Amaury Séchet 的集合哈希思路；中本聪白皮书 SPV 部分；系列前作《Why Nexa Builds Hardware》《A Node Made of Wires》。
messages.translation:
I'll fetch that Nexa forum thread and summarize it for you.# Summary of the Nexa forum post "Scaling By Circuit"

**Source**: https://forum.nexa.org/t/scaling-by-circuit/1749 (official Nexa forum, second article in the hardware project series)
Nature**: long technical article + illustrations (including 5 architecture diagrams), the core being the argument for **"achieving Bitcoin-style scaling with circuits/hardware"**, with the main arguments drawn from Nexa Chief Scientist Dr. Peter Rizun's talk at the Australian Crypto Convention in Sydney in November 2024.

---

## I. The main thread: ticking the boxes for a "better Bitcoin"

The first article in the series built Nexa's validation engine out of "six components + a tape + a head," proving it is **pipelineable**. This article ticks off the remaining three boxes, needing **only three changes**, and throws in two properties for free:

| Property | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pipelineable | Tape moves one way only | Proven in article one |
| Scalable | Parallel pipelines + "set tree" | Change #1 in this article |
| Extensible | Feedback loop → Turing machine | Derived here (an unexpected bonus) |
| Compressible | UTXO commitment written into the block header | Change #2 in this article |
| Incentive compatible | Hash function forces the full validation process to run | Topic of article one (change #3) |

---

## II. Four technical points

### 1. Two pipelines (parallelization) — solving race conditions with an "inverted clock"
- Add a second parallel validation pipeline, with a switch routing transactions to whichever one is idle.
- Difficulty one: the two heads share the same UTXO set; if both try to spend the same coin in the same clock cycle you get a **race condition**.
  - Solution (pure hardware): **invert the clock signal of the second pipeline** — one grabs coins on the rising edge, the other on the falling edge, making it physically impossible to access the same coin simultaneously. Minimalist, but very elegant.

### 2. A "set tree" replacing the Merkle tree — the key change in this article
- Difficulty two: after parallelization the **output order may differ from the input order** (TX2 may enter the block before TX1). Peer nodes recompute a different root hash → the block is judged invalid.
- The traditional fix is **sorting**, but sorting is not pipelineable (the tape would have to move back and forth) → **sorting cannot scale**.
- The author argues the "Merkle tree" in Satoshi's whitepaper should be understood by **intent rather than the letter** — what he wanted was not a "tree of a list" but a **"tree of a set."** The real answer is a **compact bitwise prefix tree**:
  - It still supports SPV proofs;
  - and is **independent of transaction order** — as long as two transaction sets are equal, the root hashes are equal.
- This builds on **Amaury Séchet**'s (BCH core developer) idea of "hashing a block as a set rather than a list."
- With it, **pipelineability is restored without sorting** → one change makes the coin "scalable."

> The scaling formula the author gives: under pipelining, the TPS ceiling ≈ **the reciprocal of the slowest step (usually signature verification)**; other short latencies don't matter; under parallelization, throughput can be **multiplied by the number of pipelines**. Rizun's own words: *"Basically we can just throw more hardware at the problem and reach any scale."*

### 3. The "accidental Turing machine" — extensibility from the feedback loop
- Scenario: Alice→Bob, and Bob immediately pays the same coin to Carol. Because ordering can't be controlled, the head may see Bob→Carol **first**: looking up the UTXO set it can't find the coin, but it can't find proof it was "spent" either → **it can be judged neither valid nor invalid = undecided**.
- Solution: add a **third pipeline** that **feeds undecided transactions back to the input**. On re-entry, Bob's coin has already been written into the UTXO set and the transaction validates normally.
- It's precisely the "existence of an undecided state" that forces a feedback path, and the feedback path lets the machine **simulate a Turing machine**: the head can move left and right, can insert new cells, and the tape length is effectively unbounded.
- Practical significance**: new features such as quantum-resistant signatures can be added **purely via script**, with **no soft or hard fork needed → the coin becomes "extensible."**

### 4. "Proofs instead of a database" — compressibility
- Status quo: fully validating nodes must maintain their own UTXO set to judge whether a coin is unspent.
- Change #2: miners store the UTXO set as a compact bitwise prefix tree and **put that tree's root hash into the block header** (right next to the block root hash).
  - The idea comes from the 2012 BitcoinTalk "ultimate blockchain compression" thread.
  - From then on, a full node only needs **one branch proof up to the block header** to confirm a coin is unspent, and **no longer needs a UTXO database**.
- Computing the UTXO root hash isn't hard for miners: it's pipelineable, parallelizable, and each insert/delete is O(log s) → it fits the definition of "scalable."

---

## III. UTXO model vs account model (Nexa vs Ethereum)

This is the closing comparison of the article, and also the root cause of "where the parallelism comes from":

| Dimension | Nexa (UTXO) | Ethereum (accounts) |
|---|---|---|
| State model | Only "coins," spent in full or not at all | Accounts + balances |
| Scope of state change | **Localized** to the specified inputs | The head sits in a global state space and can read/write anything |
| Parallelism | **High** — you can know in advance which state region each transaction can change, so multiple heads don't conflict | **Low** — the state region a transaction can touch cannot be localized |
| Risk | Inputs are essentially a "firewall" | When a contract is messy, Eve might write a transaction that deducts from Alice's account and pays Eve |
| Positioning | A coin/commodity, confirmed by miners' PoW | Ether is "shares in a decentralized company," neither a coin nor a commodity |

The author's conclusion: **they are two different things serving different purposes**; there's no simple better/worse.

---

## IV. Overall conclusion

> "On paper, this engine is already complete: a better Bitcoin, box by box ticked, made of wires and gates. What remains is to build it in **real silicon you can hold in your hand** — which is exactly where this series goes next."

**In one sentence**: this article uses **circuit-level hardware architecture** to argue why Nexa is inherently scalable — **parallel pipelines (inverted clock) + set tree (no sorting needed) + UTXO local state + feedback loop (Turing completeness) + UTXO commitment in the block header** — five things combining to yield a "scalable, extensible, compressible, incentive-compatible" improved Bitcoin, and it previews the next installment moving to **real chip implementation**.

**Cited sources**: Peter Rizun's Sydney talk (2024-11-23); the 2012 BitcoinTalk "ultimate blockchain compression" thread; Amaury Séchet's set-hashing idea; the SPV section of Satoshi's whitepaper; earlier articles in the series, "Why Nexa Builds Hardware" and "A Node Made of Wires."

summary.headline: Node 2.2.0 update notice, wallet questions, a quiet-group lament and candid price/rug talk.
summary.summary: Over roughly ten days the group was dominated by two threads. First, admin Blacktea ▽ posted the official call to upgrade to Nexa full node 2.2.0.0 (rolling checkpoints at 200 confirmations, last release before the hard fork and Tailstorm activation), which triggered a long back-and-forth with yuyuiop cvvvh about whether an uninstalled Otoplo mobile wallet needs any action — Blacktea reassured him the coins are safe and he can just reinstall the latest version when needed. Wally Wallet came up repeatedly: yuyuiop called the UI ugly, jQrgen ⛛ said Chinese translations are being improved, A-bao noted Chinese phones can't use Google Play, and Snap fingers pointed to the direct download on the official site. Second, HO HO's remark that the group is dead opened a long, informal exchange between yuyuiop cvvvh and 心存善念，万邪不侵 about the 266-member/7-online Chinese group, promotion ideas, buying another billion NEXA, the 10x on Tari (XTM), the WART project they see as a rug, and the fear of being stuck in the bag again. Blacktea also shared the 'Scaling by Circuit' hardware article and yuyuiop posted a very long (apparently AI-generated) Chinese summary of it; jQrgen added that Nexa needs no Layer 2 given 42,000 TPS on L1. Minor housekeeping: a request to kick ad bots, a spam link from 'Alex ▼', and Blacktea checking the Chinese version of the Rose /buy command.

topics.title: Price talk and rug-pull cynicism
topics.summary: yuyuiop cvvvh and 心存善念，万邪不侵 traded stories about accumulating billions of NEXA, missing the 0.0000003 bottom, a 10x on Tari (XTM), and distrust of small teams after WART went dead; the tone mixes gallows humour with hope that 'Nexa won't let everyone down'.

topics.title: Node 2.2.0.0 and Otoplo wallet
topics.summary: Blacktea ▽ announced the mandatory-ish upgrade to full node 2.2.0.0 with rolling checkpoints ahead of the hard fork and Tailstorm; yuyuiop cvvvh repeatedly asked whether his uninstalled Otoplo wallet needs updating or syncing, and Blacktea confirmed the funds can simply be left alone.

topics.title: Wally Wallet: language and Android access
topics.summary: Snap fingers recommended Wally but noted the missing Chinese, yuyuiop called the UI ugly, jQrgen ⛛ said Chinese translations are being improved and shared the site, A-bao raised that Chinese phones can't use Google Play, and Snap fingers replied it downloads directly from the official website.

topics.title: Group is too quiet / promotion
topics.summary: HO HO complained nobody is around; yuyuiop cvvvh countered that the main group is busy, noted only 7 of 266 Chinese members online, said the group needs promotion, and joked about shilling in other PoW groups and making short video skits where Nexa beats up KAS and shitcoins.

topics.title: Scaling by Circuit article
topics.summary: Blacktea ▽ shared the second hardware-series forum post on building Nexa's validation engine in circuitry (set trees, parallel pipelines, UTXO commitments); yuyuiop cvvvh posted a very long Chinese breakdown of it, and jQrgen ⛛ later argued no Layer 2 is needed because L1 already does 42,000 TPS.

topics.title: Spam bots and Rose commands
topics.summary: yuyuiop cvvvh asked Blacktea to kick ad bots after 'Alex ▼' posted an off-topic betting-league link; Blacktea also tested the Rose /buy exchange list and had yuyuiop verify the Chinese version, which he confirmed was correct.

summary.mood_description: The window starts businesslike — an upgrade announcement and patient wallet support from Blacktea ▽ — then turns wistful when HO HO points out how dead the group is. From there it becomes a frank, joking conversation between two holders about missed bottoms, a shitcoin that rugged them, and fear of being bagged again, softened by mutual encouragement to hold and wait for 'takeoff'. Underlying frustration about low activity and no Chinese-language Wally support coexists with genuine interest in the hardware-scaling research.

highlights.why: The key announcement: node 2.2.0.0 with 200-confirmation rolling checkpoints, the last release before the hard fork and Tailstorm activation.
Blunt data point on community health — only 7 of 266 Chinese group members online, prompting the promotion discussion.
Raw distrust of small crypto teams after the WART experience; captures the group's cynicism about everything except Nexa.
jQrgen's clear technical stance: no Layer 2 needed because L1 already handles 42,000 TPS, answering an earlier comment.
Practical localisation problem: Chinese users can't install Wally from Google Play, an actionable product/distribution issue.
